topics.caution: The explanation of 'ખુદાનો ભરોસો નકામ' and 'તારે ભરોસે રામ ! એ તો ખોટું' turns into a claim that ખુદા or રામ are false, or that praying to God is wrong — instead of the poet's point about NOT relying only on the divine while doing nothing oneself.
topics.guidance: Keep the explanation on શ્રમ and આત્મબળ: the poet says a person with no ભરોસો in themselves gets no real help from leaning only on ખુદા or રામ either — he names both traditions evenhandedly in his own idiom, not to argue against either faith. Let 'એકતારે ગાઈ ગાઈને' stand as the picture of a person singing instead of working; the real_life_example should stay in the child's own world (a student who only prays before an exam but never studies), never a statement about what is or isn't true of ખુદા or રામ.

chapter_level.guidance: This ગીત names both a Muslim and a Hindu term for the divine (ખુદા, રામ) in one breath, inside the poem's own self-reliance argument. Anywhere the chapter is summarised or introduced, keep both names in the poet's even-handed register — never singling one out, never framing the pair as a comparison between the two traditions, and never suggesting either belief is being mocked or contradicted. The topic is મહેનત, not theology.
